subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should source-channel delivery keep automatic bare final text as the default while hardening interim-text suppression, or should OpenClaw move direct/group/channel source replies toward explicit message-tool/final-only semantics by default?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve automatic visible replies for compatibility, while the report and later production comments show that automatic delivery can expose private reasoning or tool scaffolding in real messaging channels.

options.title: Keep automatic default, harden interim guards
options.body: Preserve existing automatic final replies for compatibility, but make interim/pre-tool/tool-adjacent text private and strengthen message_tool_only so explicit opt-in deployments get no bare-text leakage.

options.title: Flip default to explicit delivery
options.body: Make message-tool/final-only delivery the default for source channels, accepting an upgrade/migration burden for deployments that currently rely on bare-text replies.

options.title: Land only narrow candidate PRs
options.body: Review and land the current narrow fixes without deciding the default policy, leaving this canonical issue open for the remaining default-delivery question.

recommendation.title: Keep automatic default, harden interim guards
recommendation.body: Preserve existing automatic final replies for compatibility, but make interim/pre-tool/tool-adjacent text private and strengthen message_tool_only so explicit opt-in deployments get no bare-text leakage.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is a compatibility/product policy choice, and steipete appears in the merged phase-hardening history as the merger/committer for the relevant follow-up changes.
